title: Anaheim: Architecture and Algorithms for Processing Fully Homomorphic Encryption in Memory
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) workloads on GPUs are bottlenecked not by NTT (number-theoretic transform) computation but by simple element-wise modular arithmetic operations that saturate off-chip DRAM bandwidth, preventing GPUs from being practical FHE accelerators despite their computational resources.
motivation: FHE is the most promising technique for privacy-preserving cloud computing, but the DRAM bandwidth bottleneck for element-wise operations makes GPU-based FHE impractical; near-memory processing can address this directly.
method: Anaheim is a PIM (processing-in-memory) architecture for FHE that augments DRAM with versatile PIM units supporting modular integer arithmetic instructions (addition, multiplication, NTT butterfly, etc.) to execute element-wise operations in-memory, eliminating the off-chip bandwidth bottleneck. The design includes optimized FHE execution flows that partition computation between GPU (NTT-heavy phases) and PIM units (element-wise phases), efficient data mapping algorithms that exploit DRAM's internal structure (bank/row organization) to minimize data movement overhead within DRAM, and an end-to-end software framework for GPU-PIM co-execution.
key_novelty: Identifying that FHE's GPU bottleneck is element-wise operations (not NTT) and designing a PIM architecture specifically targeting these operations in DRAM, with data mapping that exploits DRAM internal bank structure to minimize in-DRAM data access overhead.
contributions: Detailed performance analysis showing element-wise modular arithmetic, not NTT, is the DRAM bandwidth bottleneck for FHE on GPUs
Versatile PIM unit design supporting multiple modular integer arithmetic instructions for FHE operators
Data mapping and PIM execution algorithms exploiting DRAM internal structure to minimize access overhead
End-to-end GPU-PIM software framework for FHE workloads with demonstrated performance and energy improvements

metrics.other: Substantial performance and energy efficiency improvement over GPU-only FHE (specific numbers not stated in abstract)

limitations: Evaluated against GPU baseline only; comparison to dedicated FHE ASICs (e.g., CraterLake, BTS) is not discussed.
primary_theme: PIM architecture for FHE element-wise modular arithmetic bottleneck relief
